text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
- An opinion survey shows that two-thirds of Romanians will spend their summer holidays at home or will visit relatives, in order to save money, the newspaper says.
- The newspaper runs a report on the auction sale of 51 percent of shares in the Petromidia oil refinery, on which a decision is still pending.
- Imported fruit juices dominate the Romanian market, according to a newspaper report.
- The newspaper quotes a survey as showing that the Romanian press netted net earnings from advertisements worth nearly $7.0 million in the past three months.
- Silviu Agapi, general manager of the state-run Romtelecom telephone operator, says in interview that the utility's privatisation will not remove the monopoly in the sector.
BURSA
- Local car maker Dacia is getting ready to join trading on the Bucharest stock exchange, the newspaper says, reporting on booming interest on the black market in shares in the Pitesti-based plant.

- Only a quarter of the 56 insurance companies registered in Romania early this year will survive under a new insurance law, due to go through parliament this autumn, the newspaper quotes a finance ministry official as saying.
- The State Ownership Fund and the reform ministry will put under their scrutiny the fate of 222 state-owned companies which have run up big debts, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL

- Romania faces for the first time a coal over-production crisis, with coal demand down 10 million tonnes from the annual demand of some 42 million tonnes, the newspaper quotes an industry ministry official as saying.
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Oil workers have postponed plans to stage a protest rally in Bucharest pending negotiations on the fate of oil refineries included on a government list of 17 firms with chronic debts, slated for closure, the newspaper says.
- The repatriation of foreign investors' profits has been simplified, says newspaper report on changes to foreign currency rules issues by Romania's National Bank.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The new National Oil Company will include only two oil refineries, the newspaper quotes a labour leader from the oil sector as saying.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania's late Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu was planning to produce a nuclear bomb, the newspaper quotes a former Securitate secret police officer as saying.

- The head of the Romanian Orthodox Church, Patriarch Teoctist, will celebrate a mass at the Putna monastery in northeast Romania on Friday, attended by visiting ex-King Michael, who is spending his summer holidays in Romania.

- Ex-Beatle Paul McCartney will be the guest of honour of the George Enescu music festival held in Bucharest in September, which will bill the premiere of his "Standing Stone" symphony, performed by the Barcelona Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Lawrence Foster, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL
- The government denies opposition accusations that it plans to return former Crown estates to ex-King Michael, the newspaper quotes government officials as saying.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
